idiom_name: SwiftUI property wrappers conforming to DynamicProperty plus ViewModifier
implementation_notes: SwiftUI has no user-defined hook functions but provides both halves of the pattern. State and effect: a property wrapper conforming to DynamicProperty is documented as a stored variable that updates an external property of a view - SwiftUI gives it values before recomputing the body - while @State, @StateObject, @Observable and @Environment cover the built-in cases and cleanup belongs to a model object's deinit or a cancelled task. Reusable behaviour: the ViewModifier protocol is the documented way to build a modifier applicable to any view, with the idiomatic form being a View extension calling modifier(_:). What replaces the classic structure (a base view class or superview owning logic for its children) is therefore a property wrapper or modifier plus an observable model; a plain @Observable model owned by @StateObject stays appropriate when state must outlive transient view identity.
pitfalls: State must live in the wrapper's @State/@StateObject storage: SwiftUI recreates view structs freely, so a plain stored property in a modifier is reinitialised and loses the state.
DynamicProperty update() runs before the view body; writing observable state from it without care can produce update loops instead of the intended refresh.
Modifiers are applied per view and are not shared - two views using the same modifier get independent state, and closures captured by the modifier must not hold stale view state.
